title: Subset Sum (Print a Subset)
statement:
You are given an array of `n` positive integers and a positive integer `target`. Decide whether some subset of the elements (each element used at most once) adds up to exactly `target`. If one exists, print one such subset; otherwise print `No subset found`.

Many subsets may qualify, so the one to print is fixed as follows. Describe a subset by the increasing list of the indices of its elements. Among all subsets with sum `target`, print the one whose index list is **lexicographically smallest** (compare the lists element by element, so a subset that uses index `0` beats any subset that does not). Print its elements in their original array order.

A subset with sum `target` is never empty, because `target ≥ 1`.
inputFormat:
The first line contains `n` and `target`.
The second line contains `n` integers, the array.
outputFormat: Print the chosen elements, in array order, separated by spaces on one line; or print `No subset found`.

examples.explanation: Several subsets add up to 9, for instance indices (2, 4) = 4 + 5. The lexicographically smallest index list is (0, 2, 5), giving 3 + 4 + 2.
Both indices (0, 1) and (2) sum to 6. (0, 1) is lexicographically smaller because it starts with index 0.
Every subset sum is even, so 5 cannot be reached.

hints: Define reach[i][s] = can the elements from index i onward form sum s? Fill it from the end of the array.
reach[i][s] is true if reach[i+1][s] is true, or if arr[i] <= s and reach[i+1][s - arr[i]] is true.
To print the subset, walk from index 0 with the remaining sum: take the first index i whose element fits and from which reach[i+1][remaining - arr[i]] is true, then continue after it.
